However, the falsification is bounded to CDN cache-key semantics (URL+Accept-Encoding excluding Authorization), not iterative decompression pipeline failure. CACHED with naive (URL, Accept-Encoding) cache key excluding Authorization is FALSIFIED-IN-SETTING (discrimination 0.0, all auth states receive same cached body). Claim bounded to: localhost mock OAuth2 server, synthetic padded JSON/HTML/XML 1KB-100KB, 4 auth states, brotli quality 6 origin, proxy re-compress quality 8, chunked TE constant background, single-layer brotli through proxy. Does NOT extend to real CDN, double/triple-brotli through proxy, Cache-Control:private/Vary:Authorization configurations, edge quality diversity, or production-scale latency.

product_action: No product action. C-MEAS-VALID remains EXPERIMENTAL. Real CDN testing required before any Product Core promotion.

reason: The frozen decision rule triggers FALSIFIED-IN-SETTING because CACHED proxy behavior has discrimination 0.0 — every auth state receives the same decompressed body. Root cause: cache key (URL, Accept-Encoding) excludes Authorization header, so first request's response is cached and served to all subsequent auth states regardless of token. This is a real and expected CDN behavior (Cloudflare/Fastly/Akamai default), not a decompression pipeline failure. Iterative decompression correctly decompresses the (wrong) cached bytes — 0 errors, all_same=true per state. The falsification is bounded and actionable: for auth-dependent content served through a CDN, the origin MUST set Cache-Control: private or Vary: Authorization to prevent stale cache serving. PASSTHROUGH (discrimination 0.5) and RECOMPRESS (discrimination 0.5) both survive, confirming decompression-normalization is format-invariant to proxy-added compression layers. The next experiment should test real CDN infrastructure with auth-aware cache configuration to resolve the blocking blocker for C-MEAS-VALID product readiness.
